finding.claim: Address6.href() interpolates the optionalPort argument into the URL without validating it. The type is number|string. A string port from untrusted input can change the URL's authority, for example `80@evil.example`, giving `http://[::1]:80@evil.example/`. The URL then has userinfo `[::1]:80` and host evil.example. Low severity because it needs the caller to forward an unvalidated string port; it is a missing-validation injection primitive that could lead to SSRF or open redirect.
finding.source: optionalPort argument of href(), a string supplied by the caller from untrusted input such as a request parameter
finding.sink: The returned URL string `http://[addr]:${port}/`, which is then fetched or redirected to by the caller

trace.note: href(optionalPort?: number | string) accepts a string
optionalPort = `:${optionalPort}` with no digit or range check
Returned as `http://[${correctForm()}]${optionalPort}/`, so `@`, `/` or `?` in the port change the URL structure

finding.guards_checked: No numeric or range check on the port in href(). fromURL() does range-check ports (ipv6.ts:245-250), but that is a separate path. The address part is built from correctForm(), so it is safe. Other HTML and URL sinks (link(), group(), AddressError.parseMessage) were checked: they escape their output, or every bad character is wrapped so no `<` can start a tag, so no XSS was found there.
